short: The plague pandemic that killed perhaps half of Europe in seven years.
full:
Arriving in the Black Sea ports in 1346 and spreading along trade routes, the Black Death reached almost every corner of Europe, North Africa and the Near East by 1353. Estimates of mortality range from a third to a half of Europe's population — somewhere between 25 and 50 million people.

The causative agent, Yersinia pestis, was not identified until 1894. Contemporary explanations ranged from miasma to divine punishment, and the search for blame produced appalling pogroms against Jewish communities. Its economic consequence was the opposite of what anyone intended: labour became scarce and therefore valuable, wages rose, and serfdom weakened decisively across western Europe.
